claim.quote: By comparing the results with three-body quantum electrodynamics calculations, we derived an antiproton-to-electron mass ratio of 1,836.1526736(23), where the parenthetical error represents one standard deviation.

name: Two-photon laser spectroscopy of antiprotonic helium and the antiproton-to-electron mass ratio

significance.quote: This agrees with the proton-to-electron value known to a similar precision.
significance.value: Three transition frequencies to fractional precisions of 2.3–5 parts in 10^9; mass ratio agrees with the proton-to-electron value

summary.plain: ASACUSA used two counter-propagating laser beams on antiprotonic helium and measured three transition frequencies to a few parts in a billion. From them it derived the antiproton-to-electron mass ratio, in agreement with the proton value.
summary.technical: Two-photon spectroscopy of 3He+ and 4He+ antiprotonic helium at 139.8, 193.0 and 197.0 nm, three transition frequencies to fractional precisions of 2.3–5 parts in 10^9; antiproton-to-electron mass ratio 1,836.1526736(23) from three-body QED, in agreement with the proton-to-electron value.

title: Two-photon laser spectroscopy of antiprotonic helium and the antiproton-to-electron mass ratio
why_it_matters: The abstract says an antimatter particle should have exactly the same mass and absolute charge as its counterpart under CPT symmetry, and that such spectroscopy can constrain the equality of the antiproton and proton charges and masses.
